The land use patterns found in the project represent an evolution of the use of project land over the years. Factors having the greatest weight in the evolution from the past pattern of almost total residential use are: (1) Out-migrations of upper and middle income groups to the suburbs, (2) In-migrations of non-whites, (3) The pressure to use properties along Second and Front Streets for commercial purposes.
Some minor land use changes in the project resulted from the Flood of 1972. These principally are the abandonment of residential property and the temporary reversion of property to vacant land. Due to fires caused by incidents related to the flooding, a number of structures in the area have been razed. Since that time these lots have not been redeveloped. Difficulties have been experienced in determining the exact number of properties that have been totally abandoned as a result of the storm. Given no public action in the area, a number of these properties would remain in an abandoned or unutalized status. It is estimated that approximately 200 properties in the project remain vacant at this time (May, 1973). As required by local law, many of these are boarded up. Present zoning of the area is represented by the existing and proposed Zoning Map, appendix G of this report. Since, for reasons given above for the deviation of land use in certain land use areas, zoning patterns indicated on the "Zoning Map," will not coincide with that of the actual land use of the area. However, general simularities between land use and zoning can be noted. An explanation of the uses permitted under the existing zoning designation for the Project area is included with appendix G.
b. Population
The project area has principally two types of residents, (1) those whose permanent domicile is that of the project area and (2) those who own businesses or work in the area and live elsewhere.
Approximately 3,600 persons classed under (1) above, live within the project area. Their distribution, density and age characteristics are shown on The Approximate Flood Level Map, appendix A. The racial character of the project's population is discussed separately.
Those classed under (2) above are not true residents in the strickest definition of the term. They do represent, however, a large part of the community during working hours, and, therefore, are considered in somewhat the same context as permanent residents for discussion purposes.
